summary: Mission Architect: Beyond Earth is a 3D space mission design game built with Godot. Players design a spacecraft, plan a mission, launch a rocket, and operate a satellite while balancing power, communications, science objectives, and mission reliability. The game brings space science to life through orbital mechanics, launch and ascent physics, procedural planetary environments, and live NASA data, including EONET natural-event reports and TEMPO air-quality measurements. By combining interactive mission planning with real scientific concepts and datasets, the project helps players explore how space missions work and how satellite observations can support our understanding of Earth and other worlds.
details:
Mission Architect: Beyond Earth is a 3D space mission design game built in Godot Engine using GDScript. It allows players to design a spacecraft, plan a mission, launch a rocket through realistic ascent physics, and operate a satellite while managing power, communications, science objectives, and mission reliability.

The game addresses the challenge of making space science accessible and engaging. It integrates live NASA data, including EONET natural-event reports and TEMPO NO2 air-quality measurements, so players can base missions on real-world observations. The simulation uses orbital mechanics, gravity-turn launch dynamics, atmospheric drag, and eclipse-aware power systems to provide an authentic experience.

Benefits include hands-on learning about mission design, satellite operations, and Earth observation. We used Godot 4, GDScript, NASA public APIs, and procedural 3D environments. The project is creative because it combines real scientific data with interactive gameplay rather than passive learning. We prioritized scientific accuracy, educational impact, and accessibility, ensuring the game runs offline with cached NASA data while remaining engaging for both students and space enthusiasts.
